description:
FILED + FIXED s473t5f (#1501 round 7, uni/, 2026-09-13).

THE BUG, a SILENT WRONG.  `in-package` is read-time and cannot re-home the
symbols around it (reference_in_package_is_read_time), so a package global
WRITTEN inside a nested `{ package X; â¦ }` block must be emitted QUALIFIED.
`Pl::Parser2::_requalify_region`'s word-shaped name class was
`/^[A-Za-z_]\w*$/` -- ASCII ONLY -- so a non-ASCII name was skipped and the
WRITE came out bare while every READ of the same global came out qualified:

    use utf8; no strict;
    { { package Abc4; $ãÄ½uá¹fâ³ = 5; }
      print defined $Abc4::ãÄ½uá¹fâ³ ? $Abc4::ãÄ½uá¹fâ³ : 'undef', "\n"; }
    # perl: 5     PCL: undef

    emitted:  (p-scalar-= |$ãÄ½uá¹fâ³| 5)        <- bare, lands in MAIN
              (p-defined Abc4::|$ãÄ½uá¹fâ³|)     <- qualified, reads Abc4

The ASCII twin is `(p-scalar-= Abc4::$blurfl 5)` and is right, which is why it
took a non-ASCII population to find.  Same family as #313 (GlobalPartition
matched a segment's first character ASCII-only) and #1650 (an all-digit
container name) -- a name CLASS written ASCII-only in one of the sites that
must agree about what a name is.

THE DISCRIMINATOR, measured: the failing shape needs the nested package block
to sit inside a BARE BLOCK (at FILE level the declaration is qualified by a
different path and the write is right).  Four-way probe: ASCII pkgs +
non-ASCII var FAILS, non-ASCII pkgs + ASCII var PASSES, both non-ASCII FAILS,
no enclosing statement-switch FAILS -- so it is the VARIABLE name's class, not
the package's.

THE FIX.  `/^[^\W\d]\w*\z/` -- the spelling `$VAR_TOKEN_RX`'s pipe-quoted
alternative already uses, Unicode-aware on a decoded string and a strict
superset of the old class on ASCII.  ONE character class, ONE site: the other
requalifier (`_requalify_block_our_after_pkg_switch`) already tests `\w`, and
the two other `[A-Za-z_]\w*` occurrences in Parser2 are a disqualifier scan
and $VAR_TOKEN_RX itself, neither on this axis.  An all-DIGIT container name
(#1650) stays excluded, as it always was.

WHAT IT MOVED.  t/uni/package.t (3 of its 10 blessed rows -- `comp/stash.t
test 4/5/7`, `$ìÆ::ãÄ½uá¹fâ³` read as 5) and, in the SHAPES corpus,
`Pl/t/shapes/interpolation-nonascii.pl` S08 and S11: their `our @ï¼¸` /
`our %ï¼¨` / `$#ï¼¸` had BOTH the write and the interpolated read going to
MAIN, so the file's own output agreed with perl BY ACCIDENT.  That is what the
SHAPES population (#496) exists to catch, and corpus-diff's SHAPES line is
what caught it.

BARS.  corpus-diff vs 347a46e3: emission identical over the 111-file corpus,
SHAPES 1 of 6 differs (explained above); emission A/B 571 files 567 SAME /
4 DIFF / 0 RCDIFF -- the shapes file, uni/package.t, and #1736's two.
Generation v2-1360 -> v2-1460 with all three artifacts regenerated.  Guard
`Pl/t/utf8-source-01.t` row 9 (all three container sigils + a `my` negative),
inverse-verified FAILING on a 347a46e3 extraction.  A NAME-RESOLUTION change,
so the full sweep IS the gate (see the round record) and the gate-SET scan was
run over both populations.
subject: SILENT WRONG: a non-ASCII package global WRITTEN inside a nested `package X` block is emitted UNQUALIFIED while every read of it is qualified -- _requalify_region word-shaped name class was ASCII-only (FIXED s473t5f)
